lines: Five effect loops, each switching between sending its input out to a chain and taking it back, and passing that input straight through
Lit, that line's in jack goes to the SEND jack beside it and its ret. jack goes to OUT; unlit, in goes straight to OUT and SEND is held at 0V
Lit, that line's two in jacks go to the two SEND jacks beside them and its two ret. jacks to its two OUT jacks; unlit, each in goes straight to the OUT on its row and both SEND jacks are held at 0V
Lit, the in jack goes to SEND and the two ret. jacks go to the two OUT jacks; unlit, the in jack is copied to both OUT jacks at 0.71 of its level and SEND is held at 0V
The signal into that row, polyphonic channels and all; it goes to the SEND jack beside it while the button is lit, and to the OUT jack on the same row while it is unlit
The mono signal into the bottom line; while its button is unlit it is copied to both OUT jacks at 0.71 of its level, a centre pan that keeps the pair at the same apparent loudness
That row's send out to an effect chain, carrying the in jack beside it while the button is lit and held at 0V while it is unlit
The return from that row's effect chain, passed to the OUT jack beside it while the button is lit; while the button is unlit nothing here is read
That row's output: the ret. jack beside it while the button is lit, and the in jack on the same row while it is unlit
The left output of the bottom line: its ret. jack while the button is lit, and the in jack at 0.71 of its level while it is unlit
The right output of the bottom line: its ret. jack while the button is lit, and the in jack at 0.71 of its level while it is unlit
Note — every button comes up unlit, so each line passes its input straight to its output and every SEND jack is held at 0V until a button is pressed.
Note — the bottom line takes one mono in jack and gives two OUT jacks, and its two ret. jacks bring back a stereo effect.
Note — a jack is written only when the input feeding it is patched as well; an output whose source is unpatched is held at 0V.
Note — bypassing the whole module in Rack passes each in jack to the OUT jack on its own row.

Bypass.notes: No port families are given: the module routes whatever is patched into it, audio or CV alike. There is no in jack for the fifteenth row, because the bottom line is mono into stereo: one input, one send, two returns and two outputs. The plugin's own bypass mapping (configBypass) covers inputs 0 to 6 against outputs 0 to 6, so Rack's bypass leaves the bottom line's right output silent.

lines: Constant-power panner placing a polyphonic mono signal between a left and a right output
Places the signal between the two outputs, hard left at one end and hard right at the other, with both outputs at 0.71 of the input level at the centre
The signal to be panned; every polyphonic channel is panned and the outputs carry the same number of channels
Added to the PAN knob channel by channel; with the knob hard left, 0V to 10V here sweeps left to right, and with the knob centred, -5V to +5V does
The input scaled by the cosine of the pan angle, full level with the pan hard left and silent with it hard right
The input scaled by the sine of the pan angle, silent with the pan hard left and full level with it hard right
Note — with nothing patched to in, both outputs are held at 0V.
Note — the CV jack is read channel by channel against the in jack's channel count, so a monophonic CV cable pans only the first channel and every other channel follows the knob alone.
Note — bypassing the whole module in Rack passes in straight to the left output and leaves the right one silent.

Pan.notes: The knob is ±5V and the CV is summed with it before a single clamp, so the pair behaves as one control clamped to ±5V rather than as a knob with an attenuated CV. The README says the CV input is polyphonic, which it is, but it is read against the in jack's channel count: a mono CV cable leaves every channel past the first following the knob alone.
